data.title: Social welfare caseload
data.question: How many cases is the office carrying, and in what state?

data.title: Assistance pipeline
data.question: Where are assistance requests sitting on their way to a decision?

data.title: Case aging and turnaround
data.question: How long have open requests been waiting?
data.caution: Waiting time, not lateness. The office has adopted no service standard for these, so nothing here is behind a target.

data.title: Field visit workload
data.question: How many visits are scheduled, done, or not completed?

data.title: Staff workload
data.question: How is open work distributed across the office right now?
data.caution: This counts what each person is carrying so work can be moved. It is not a productivity measure and must not be read as one: a heavy caseload is usually a hard caseload, and the office cannot see from a count who is doing well.

data.title: Programme utilisation
data.question: Which programmes are being used, and how much has gone out?

data.title: Release and distribution status
data.question: What has been released, what is waiting, and what could not be paid?

data.title: Referral outcomes
data.question: What happened to the people this office referred elsewhere?

data.title: Beneficiaries by barangay
data.question: Where in the municipality is assistance reaching people?

data.title: Household vulnerability indicators
data.question: Which indicators are present across the households on file?
data.caution: Indicators are evidence a caseworker reads, never a decision. Nothing here ranks households or establishes entitlement.

data.title: Demographic service reach
data.question: Which sectors is the office reaching, and which it may be missing?
data.caution: Sector membership is sensitive. Figures small enough to identify somebody are withheld rather than shown.

data.title: Repeat assistance patterns
data.question: How often do households come back, and how soon?
data.caution: A household returning is a fact about their circumstances, not about them. This exists for planning, and it decides nobody’s eligibility.

data.title: Requirements bottlenecks
data.question: Which documents hold applications up most often?

data.title: Data completeness and verification
data.question: Which records are missing something the office needs?
data.person_level_justification: A completeness report is worked through record by record. A count cannot be acted on — somebody has to open each named record and fill in what is missing.
data.caution: This report names people, because it exists to be corrected record by record. Do not circulate it outside the office.
